notes: THREE categories of SNOMED allergy code live in this ONE list, distinguished by `category` -- all matched, flagged, and (when safe) ended by the exact same mechanism in content-scripts/allergy-cleanup.js, so there's no reason to split them into separate files. `category:"import-artefact"` entries are NEVER a genuine allergy record under any circumstances -- pure import noise, safe to bulk-end outright. `category:"too-generic"` entries ARE occasionally used to carry a real allergy, just coded uselessly vaguely -- e.g. a real patient's peanut allergy found coded as free-text "peanut" in additionalInformation under 419076005 "Allergic reaction" rather than an actual substance code. These are NOT automatically safe to end: the widget's existing per-instance caution mechanism (buildCautionMessage, keyed on additionalInformation/severity/certainty/allergyReactions being populated) is what makes including them here safe at all -- a too-generic code with NOTHING else attached is genuinely useless noise and gets offered for bulk-end same as an import-artefact entry, but the moment ANY clinical detail is attached, caution fires, the row is excluded from 'Select all', and the clinician has to look at it individually before deciding. `category:"low-prescribing-relevance"` (added 2026-08-02, following the substance-conversion CSV review) is DIFFERENT again: these are genuine, correctly-coded allergies -- not import noise, not miscoded -- that are simply of near-zero relevance to the allergy list's real purpose (prescribing safety), e.g. 300910009 "Allergy to pollen" (hay fever) will never affect a prescribing decision the way a drug/food allergy would. These entries carry a per-CODE `caution` string (a NEW field, distinct from the per-instance buildCautionMessage signal -- ALWAYS shown for every entry of this code, regardless of what clinical detail is or isn't attached, softening the framing from "remove this junk" to "this may be more appropriate as a problem code") and are, same as any cautioned row, excluded from 'Select all' -- always an individual clinician decision, never bulk. FUTURE WORK, explicitly deferred, not built yet: when a too-generic code carries a real allergen in its free text (the peanut example), the useful move isn't to end it at all -- it's to CONVERT it to a proper substance-coded allergy using that free text as a search hint, an extension of the same idea as the caution mechanism, not yet designed. Matched by EXACT conceptId only (never a hierarchy/descendant search) for ALL THREE categories -- unlike rules/non-problem-root-codes.json's admin-code roots (broad categories with many real children needing a descendant search), each entry here is a single, self-contained SNOMED concept, not a root with meaningful children. Used by content-scripts/allergy-cleanup.js's 'Clean up allergies?' widget: fetches every ACTIVE allergy's own conceptId via GET clinical/data/allergy/overview-allergy/{allergyId} (the cheap clinical-summary/summary list has no conceptId, text only) and flags an exact match against this list. Each entry's own `reasonEnded` is submitted verbatim to POST clinical/allergy/end-allergy -- confirmed live 2026-07-29 that endpoint's payload is just {allergyId, endDate, reasonEnded}, with NO recordedByOrganisation field at all, so ending a junk allergy is never blocked by the blank-organisation validation lock that DOES affect converting one via change-allergy. Add a new entry only once a real patient's allergy list has confirmed it -- same discipline as every other code list in this codebase, never guess a plausible-sounding sibling in. NOTE (2026-08-02 pre-merge review): a per-code `caution` string may appear on an entry of ANY category, not just low-prescribing-relevance -- e.g. 716186003 "No known allergies" is category import-artefact (its duplicates are pure import noise) but carries a caution because removing the LAST copy destroys a genuine clinical assertion; any cautioned entry is excluded from 'Select all' regardless of category.

codes.caution: This code is a positive record that allergy status was checked and found nil -- removing the LAST remaining copy makes the record read as "never asked", which is clinically different from "asked, none found" (and it's what goes out on GP2GP). Remove surplus duplicate copies only; keep one.
codes.rationale: Confirmed live via overview-allergy (real patient), and independently reported by the user as a recurring pattern: a pre-defined allergy CODE recording the ABSENCE of allergies, frequently duplicated several times over a patient's import history (five identical copies confirmed on one real patient's clinical-summary list). The DUPLICATES are pure noise -- but the code itself is NOT (2026-08-02 pre-merge review, Virtual Dave must-fix A): unlike an empty list ("nobody asked"), a coded NKA entry asserts "asked, and the answer was nil", and Medicus's rendered empty state can't carry that distinction onto a GP2GP transfer. So this entry carries a per-code caution (same mechanism as the low-prescribing-relevance category): always excluded from 'Select all', every removal an individual decision, with the caution text steering toward de-duplication rather than deletion to zero.

codes.reasonEnded: Too generic to be clinically useful -- a historic non-drug-allergy marker that does not identify an actual allergen, and carried no other clinical detail
codes.rationale: Confirmed by the user (2026-07-29), not yet independently live-captured via overview-allergy for this specific concept (add a live confirmation note here once seen directly). Per the user: a historic marker code from a locally-commissioned service, erroneously pulled into the actual allergy list by the import/GP2GP process (or possibly by Medicus itself), often duplicated a dozen or so times across a patient's record history. RECATEGORISED import-artefact -> too-generic (2026-08-02 pre-merge review, Virtual Dave must-fix B): the code's own SNOMED semantics are a POSITIVE finding -- "patient HAS a history of a non-drug allergy" -- not an "allergies were asked about" marker, so an instance of it can be the only surviving trace of a real latex/bee-sting/food allergy that never got a substance code. The too-generic per-instance caution mechanism (buildCautionMessage) is exactly the right protection: an instance with NOTHING attached is bulk-endable noise, but the moment any clinical detail is attached the row is excluded from 'Select all' and needs an individual decision.

codes.reasonEnded: Too generic to be clinically useful -- covers almost every allergic condition without identifying an actual allergen, and carried no other clinical detail
codes.rationale: Confirmed by the user (2026-07-29): "Atopy" covers almost everything allergic -- coding an allergy this way conveys essentially no information about what the patient is actually allergic to. UNLIKE the import-artefact entries above, this code CAN legitimately carry a real allergy (e.g. via additionalInformation free text) -- see the top-level `notes` for the real peanut-allergy example that motivated adding this whole category, and buildCautionMessage's own comment for the mechanism that makes bulk-ending this specific code safe: it's only ever offered when NOTHING else is attached to the entry.

codes.reasonEnded: Too generic to be clinically useful -- does not identify an actual allergen, and carried no other clinical detail
codes.rationale: Confirmed by the user (2026-07-29), and the DIRECT motivating example for the whole `too-generic` category: a real patient's peanut allergy was found coded under this concept with the allergen recorded only as free-text "peanut" in additionalInformation -- exactly the case buildCautionMessage's caution mechanism exists to protect (that entry would be flagged amber and excluded from 'Select all', never bulk-ended). Like Atopy, this code says only that SOME reaction to SOMETHING occurred, without identifying what -- useful only as a placeholder pending a proper substance code, never a genuinely complete allergy record on its own.

codes.reasonEnded: Coded as an allergy but represents hay fever (environmental pollen sensitivity), not relevant to prescribing safety -- recommend recording as a problem instead if clinically significant
codes.caution: This code indicates hay fever, so may be more appropriate as a problem code rather than an allergy.
codes.rationale: Explicit user reasoning (2026-08-02), spotted during the substance-conversion CSV review: this IS a genuine, correctly-coded allergy (technically real, IgE-mediated) -- not import noise, not miscoded like gluten enteropathy/intolerance -- but functionally it's hay fever, which will almost never affect a prescribing decision, the actual purpose of the allergy section. Softened wording deliberately mirrors the `TEXT:` advisory-note pattern already used for similar judgement-call entries in vtm-auto-resolution.csv (e.g. "Fixed oil") -- a suggestion to reconsider, not a flat claim the code is wrong.
